reviewers.summary: The manuscript is a placeholder that lacks the core numeric result, variable definitions, assumptions checks, and necessary methodological details. The analysis (Pearson correlation) is not adequately reported and the claims cannot be evaluated.

findings.title: Primary result omitted from manuscript
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript fails to state the correlation coefficient (r=0.658) and p-value, making it impossible to assess the study's main finding. This omission prevents any meaningful review or interpretation.
findings.actionableFix: Add the Pearson correlation coefficient, its 95% confidence interval, p-value, and sample size to the Results section and Abstract.
findings.deterministicVerification: Check that the manuscript now contains numeric output from stats-run.json (correlation=0.6579, p=3.87e-31, n=240).

findings.title: No verification of Pearson correlation assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: Pearson correlation assumes linearity, bivariate normality, and absence of influential outliers. Without checks, the estimated r=0.658 may be misleading.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a scatterplot with LOESS smoother, test for normality (Shapiro-Wilk), and report outlier diagnostics. If assumptions fail, consider Spearman correlation or transformation.

findings.title: Variable definitions and measurement missing
findings.whyItMatters: Without knowing what 'severity' and 'outcome_cont' represent (e.g., clinical scale, units, range), the clinical relevance and potential floor/ceiling effects cannot be judged.
findings.actionableFix: Describe each variable: what it measures, how it was collected, its possible range, and any known validation. Provide summary statistics (mean, SD, min, max).

findings.title: No adjustment for potential confounders
findings.whyItMatters: Observational association can be confounded. Even if no causal claim is made, the raw correlation may over- or underestimate the true relationship and limits the interpretation of the strength of linear association.
findings.actionableFix: Either adjust for known confounders (if available) or explicitly state that no confounders were measured and discuss this as a key limitation in the Discussion.

findings.title: Missing data handling not described
findings.whyItMatters: The analysis uses 240 complete cases, but the original sample size and proportion of missingness are unknown. Non-random missingness could bias the correlation.
findings.actionableFix: Report the initial sample size, number excluded for missing data, and compare demographics of excluded vs. included subjects if possible. If not, acknowledge as limitation.

findings.title: Ethical approval and data provenance not stated
findings.whyItMatters: Medical/public-health studies must disclose ethical review and data source per reporting guidelines (e.g., STROBE).
findings.actionableFix: Add a statement on institutional review board (IRB) approval or exemption, and source of the dataset.

missingEvidence: Assumptions checks for Pearson correlation (linearity, normality, outliers)

reviewers.summary: Essential Pearson correlation assumption checks (linearity, normality, outliers, homoscedasticity) are absent from the diagnostics artifact and not described. Without these, the reported correlation (r=0.658, p<0.001) is untrustworthy. The report also lacks a confidence interval, missingness analysis, and data plausibility review. The manuscript incorrectly claims QA issues were found when none are recorded. Analysis must be rerun with proper diagnostics and reporting before any claims.

findings.title: No diagnostic checks for Pearson correlation assumptions
findings.whyItMatters: Pearson requires linearity, bivariate normality, and homoscedasticity. Violations can invalidate the correlation coefficient and p-value.
findings.actionableFix: Run and document diagnostic plots (residuals vs. fitted, Q-Q), normality tests (Shapiro-Wilk), and consider robust alternatives (e.g., Spearman) if violations are present.

findings.title: Diagnostics artifact contains only test name and sample size
findings.whyItMatters: No evidence that assumption checks were performed or inspected, making the analysis irreproducible and the result suspect.
findings.actionableFix: Extend the diagnostics.json to include numeric and visual results for normality, linearity, and outlier detection.

findings.title: Confidence interval for correlation not reported
findings.whyItMatters: A point estimate (0.658) alone is insufficient; a 95% CI communicates the precision of the estimate and is essential for interpretation.
findings.actionableFix: Compute and report a 95% confidence interval for the Pearson correlation coefficient.

findings.title: No description of missing data handling or complete-case exclusions
findings.whyItMatters: Complete-case analysis can introduce selection bias if missingness is related to exposure or outcome; readers cannot assess the impact without details.
findings.actionableFix: Report number of records excluded, reasons, compare included/excluded groups on available variables, and discuss potential bias.

findings.title: No evidence of data range, distribution, or outlier inspection
findings.whyItMatters: Non-normal distributions or extreme outliers can distort Pearson correlation, yet the data are unchecked.
findings.actionableFix: Provide summary statistics (min, max, mean, SD, skewness) and visualizations (histograms, boxplots) before correlation.

findings.title: Manuscript states advisory issues found, but QA records show none
findings.whyItMatters: Creates confusion: either the manuscript is outdated, or the QA process missed real issues. Inconsistent reporting undermines trust.
findings.actionableFix: If real issues exist, list them; otherwise, remove the generic advisory warning from the manuscript.

findings.title: Extremely small p-value reported without effect size interpretation
findings.whyItMatters: A p-value of 3.87e-31 does not convey practical significance; the manuscript fails to contextualize the correlation magnitude (e.g., R² = 0.43).
findings.actionableFix: Add interpretation of the correlation strength (e.g., 'large effect') and its practical meaning, along with the CI.

findings.title: Figure caption lacks descriptive detail
findings.whyItMatters: The caption 'Scatterplot for the two variables used in the correlation run' does not guide interpretation or mention observed trend.
findings.actionableFix: Revise caption to note the linear association, strength, and any notable patterns (e.g., 'strong positive linear relationship, r = 0.66').

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
